Illinois Fighting Illini.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide for Bret Bielema. The guide does record the incoming defensive coordinator's head-coaching background: Bobby Hauck arrives after an eight-year second spell as Montana head coach.
Illinois Fighting Illini.dc: Bobby Hauck, in from Montana after Aaron Henry left for Notre Dame.
Illinois Fighting Illini.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Illinois Fighting Illini.dc_status: New — the guide records Aaron Henry leaving for Notre Dame and Hauck arriving, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Illinois Fighting Illini.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme, though the guide describes a new system for the incoming quarterback and names it as one of two offsetting risks.
Illinois Fighting Illini.defensive_scheme: Named. The guide describes Hauck installing a new 3-3-5 defense and allows the scheme could catch opponents by surprise.
Illinois Fighting Illini.run_pass: Stated as an identity the results do not match. The guide records that Illinois prides itself on old-school physical Big Ten football under Bielema, yet ranked 13th in the conference rushing at 138.1 yards per game.
Illinois Fighting Illini.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide judges Katin Houser has a better supporting cast in Champaign than he had at Michigan State, while flagging the new system and a rebuilt line against him.
Illinois Fighting Illini.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback both change. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 9.
Illinois Fighting Illini.staff_turnover: Concentrated on defense: Aaron Henry left for Notre Dame and Hauck was hired to reinvent what the guide calls a stale defense.
Illinois Fighting Illini.prior_school: Montana for Hauck. On the roster the guide records Katin Houser returning to the Big Ten from East Carolina having previously been at Michigan State, and Wisconsin center Jake Renfro arriving as the only Power Four transfer on the line.
Illinois Fighting Illini.portal_recruiting: Tied directly to the staff. The guide rates Bielema among the country's better evaluators and developers of linemen, then cautions that he imported only one Power Four transfer for a line replacing four starters, and notes the defensive line's five departing rotational players are replaced by Group of Six or FCS talent.
Illinois Fighting Illini.vsin_assessment: Credit for the record, scepticism about the identity. The guide notes Illinois won 19 games across the last two seasons, the most in programme history over a two-year span, then sets out a gap between identity and output — an old-school physical programme that ranked 13th in the Big Ten rushing and 12th in scoring defense at 23.6 points allowed.
Illinois Fighting Illini.strengths: A head coach the guide rates among the country's better evaluators and developers of offensive linemen, a coordinator hire with top-20 FCS scoring defenses and top-10 takeaway finishes in three of the last five years, four returning senior defensive backs including All-Big Ten free safety Xavier Scott, and a new scheme the guide says could catch opponents by surprise.
Illinois Fighting Illini.concerns: A defensive line replacing five rotational players including second-round pick Gabe Jacas with Group of Six and FCS talent — which the guide calls the roster's biggest question — a line already overmatched against better fronts, and a new quarterback learning a new system behind it.
Illinois Fighting Illini.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Indiana Hoosiers.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide directly. The guide records that many of the departing players were the James Madison players who came with Curt Cignetti.
Indiana Hoosiers.dc: Bryant Haines, a Broyles Award winner.
Indiana Hoosiers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator, and the guide states Cignetti kept his staff intact.
Indiana Hoosiers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator, and six starters return for Haines.
Indiana Hoosiers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The guide attributes the scheme decision jointly to Cignetti and coordinator Mike Shanahan.
Indiana Hoosiers.offensive_scheme: Addressed as a stated adjustment rather than a named system: the guide expects Cignetti and Shanahan to run less RPO because Josh Hoover lacks Fernando Mendoza's size and athleticism.
Indiana Hoosiers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Indiana Hoosiers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated tendency beyond the reduced RPO usage.
Indiana Hoosiers.qb_development: Addressed as an environment rather than a coaching record: the guide argues Indiana's setting should fix much of Hoover's ball-security problem, noting no FBS team has fewer giveaways over the last two seasons than Indiana's 17.
Indiana Hoosiers.continuity: Complete on the staff, broken at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 3 for 16 returning starters, totalling 13.
Indiana Hoosiers.staff_turnover: None. The guide's specific phrase is that Cignetti kept his staff intact.
Indiana Hoosiers.prior_school: James Madison, which the guide raises as a culture question — many of the departures were the James Madison players who came with Cignetti. On the roster it records Josh Hoover from TCU, Nick Marsh from Michigan State and Turbo Richard from Boston College.
Indiana Hoosiers.portal_recruiting: Tied to a stated coaching philosophy. The guide cites Cignetti's preference for production over potential, records eight further Power Four starters added through the portal, and names TCU's Josh Hoover as the active FBS passing leader with 9,629 yards and 71 touchdowns.
Indiana Hoosiers.vsin_assessment: Confident in the staff, open on the culture. Against a programme-record eight draft picks lost including Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza, the guide's judgement is that the cupboard is not bare, resting on an intact staff, 10 returning starters and a portal haul. It expects Cignetti to keep operating with a chip on his shoulder to prove 2025 was not a fluke, and leaves open whether the culture can sustain this or was lightning in a bottle.
Indiana Hoosiers.strengths: Total staff continuity behind a Broyles Award-winning defensive coordinator with six starters back, arguably the best offensive line in college football, the fewest giveaways in FBS over two seasons, and a head coach the guide expects to thrive on doubt.
Indiana Hoosiers.concerns: Replacing a Heisman winner and No. 1 overall pick plus seven other draft picks, a quarterback with 33 turnovers in 36 career games, and a culture question the guide raises explicitly — whether it holds now that the James Madison core has left and Indiana is the hunted rather than the hunter.
Indiana Hoosiers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Iowa Hawkeyes.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide as prior head-coaching experience. The guide records that Kirk Ferentz enters his 28th season, is the Big Ten's longest-tenured coach, and passed Woody Hayes last season as the conference's all-time winningest coach.
Iowa Hawkeyes.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Iowa Hawkeyes.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Iowa Hawkeyes.play_caller: Not addressed in guide. The guide records that coordinator Tim Lester chooses the starting quarterback between Hank Brown and Jeremy Hecklinski.
Iowa Hawkeyes.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide expects Iowa to lean on a talented line and the running back tandem given the quarterback inexperience.
Iowa Hawkeyes.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide records Iowa ranking top-10 nationally in scoring, passing and total defense with a 17th-ranked run defense.
Iowa Hawkeyes.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy, but the guide sets the passing offense's national rankings of 129th, 130th and 130th over the last three seasons as the standing problem and expects a run-leaning approach.
Iowa Hawkeyes.qb_development: Not addressed as a development record. The guide records instead that Iowa has leaned on the portal for starters in recent seasons, most recently Mark Gronowski from North Dakota State.
Iowa Hawkeyes.continuity: Complete at head coach and both coordinators, broken at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 11.
Iowa Hawkeyes.staff_turnover: One departure the guide treats as significant: special teams coordinator LeVar Woods, on Ferentz's staff since 2008 and coordinator since 2018, left for the same role plus an assistant head coach title under Pat Fitzgerald at Michigan State. Chris Polizzi is promoted in his place.
Iowa Hawkeyes.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records L.J. Phillips arriving from South Dakota with 1,920 yards and 19 touchdowns in 2025.
Iowa Hawkeyes.portal_recruiting: Presented as a change in method. Iowa replaces 27 seniors, 16 of them starters — the largest roster turnover of the Ferentz era — and responds with a programme-record 16 transfers, which the guide presents as an acknowledgement that development alone is no longer sufficient.
Iowa Hawkeyes.vsin_assessment: The benefit of the doubt, explicitly earned. The guide gives the staff that benefit despite an inexperienced quarterback and many new faces on defense and special teams, resting on Ferentz's floor — never fewer than eight wins since 2015 apart from 2020 and 2023, when two wins were vacated over tampering with quarterback Cade McNamara before he entered the portal. It treats Phil Parker as one of the best coordinators in the game and says he earned the benefit of the doubt long ago.
Iowa Hawkeyes.strengths: The Big Ten's longest-tenured and all-time winningest coach with a 13-year winning streak, a defensive coordinator the guide rates among the best in the game, an annually elite special-teams unit, and a talented offensive line.
Iowa Hawkeyes.concerns: A quarterback room of Hank Brown, with one Auburn start two years ago, and Jeremy Hecklinski, with two career attempts, fronting a passing offense ranked 129th, 130th and 130th in three seasons; only three defensive starters back with six of the top eight linemen gone; and the loss of a special-teams coordinator of 18 years' standing.
Iowa Hawkeyes.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Maryland Terrapins.oc: Clint Trickett, in from a season as coordinator at Jacksonville State; Pep Hamilton moves to an advisory role.
Maryland Terrapins.dc: Ted Monachino, in his second season.
Maryland Terrapins.oc_status: New — the guide records the move of Pep Hamilton to an advisory role and Trickett taking over, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Maryland Terrapins.dc_status: Returning — Monachino enters his second season with eight starters back, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Maryland Terrapins.play_caller: Changed on offense. Trickett takes over the coordinator's job with Hamilton moved upstairs.
Maryland Terrapins.offensive_scheme: Stated as a specific set of intentions rather than a named system: the guide records Trickett wanting more RPO, more designed running from Malik Washington, and increased tempo through more motion and more snaps.
Maryland Terrapins.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide's summary of the unit is that Maryland can clearly rush the passer but has struggled to stop the run inside.
Maryland Terrapins.tempo: Stated and increasing — the guide records Trickett wanting increased tempo through more motion and more snaps.
Maryland Terrapins.run_pass: Addressed as a stated shift toward the run: more RPO and more designed quarterback running, against a 2025 team that ranked second-to-last in the Big Ten at 104.3 rushing yards per game, 122nd nationally.
Maryland Terrapins.qb_development: Addressed through the incoming coordinator's plan and the returning starter's freshman year. The guide credits Washington with about all you could ask of a true freshman starting in the Big Ten — just under 3,000 passing yards, a 17-to-9 touchdown-to-interception ratio and four rushing scores — and calls him a potential star conditional on more production around him.
Maryland Terrapins.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 3 for 16 returning starters, totalling 14.
Maryland Terrapins.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive side, and internal in part — Hamilton moves to an advisory role rather than leaving.
Maryland Terrapins.prior_school: Jacksonville State for Trickett. The guide records Monachino's professional background: he was on the Ravens staff that won Super Bowl XLVII and coached Terrell Suggs and Elvis Dumervil, which it treats as evidence he knows elite front-seven talent.
Maryland Terrapins.portal_recruiting: Tied to the head coach. The guide credits Mike Locksley as a high-level recruiter who has kept DMV talent home, cites five-star Baltimore freshman Zion Elee, and records Harry Dalton III transferring in from USC.
Maryland Terrapins.vsin_assessment: Hot seat, with credit attached. The guide places Locksley on the hot seat after consecutive 4-8 seasons, records the collapse — 4-0, then three losses by four points or fewer, then an eight-game losing streak — and states bluntly that he cannot live off the 23-16 run from 2021 to 2023 forever, while crediting him as a high-level recruiter who has kept local talent home.
Maryland Terrapins.strengths: 71% of production returning, second nationally to Notre Dame per ESPN's Bill Connelly; a returning quarterback the guide calls a potential star; a coordinator with a Super Bowl pedigree entering his second season with eight starters back; and a head coach the guide rates as a high-level recruiter.
Maryland Terrapins.concerns: A head coach on the hot seat after two 4-8 seasons, a new offensive coordinator installing a different system, no 1,000-yard rusher since 2022, poor run blocking, a receiving corps plagued by drops, and a defense that struggles to stop the run inside.
Maryland Terrapins.betting: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins, argued partly through the staff: the guide credits Locksley's recruiting and Monachino's second-year defense while stating he cannot live off the 2021-23 run forever.

Michigan State Spartans.previous_hc_experience: Extensive and central to the hire. The guide records Pat Fitzgerald as Northwestern's all-time winningest coach and a College Football Hall of Famer, notes he was terminated at his alma mater three years ago after significant hazing allegations were reported, sued for wrongful termination and settled last August, clearing his return, and records that he was a volunteer coach at his son's high school for the last three seasons.
Michigan State Spartans.oc: Nick Sheridan, in from the same role at Alabama.
Michigan State Spartans.oc_status: New — the guide records Sheridan arriving from Alabama, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Michigan State Spartans.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Michigan State Spartans.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name for 2026.
Michigan State Spartans.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide's stated expectation is that the run game, led by UConn transfer Cam Edwards, will have to carry more.
Michigan State Spartans.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Michigan State Spartans.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy, but the guide expects the run game to carry more given the receiving losses.
Michigan State Spartans.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide expects the incumbent Alessio Milivojevic — 986 yards in four starts — to hold the job for Fitzgerald and Sheridan over Cam Fancher's 28 starts across Marshall, Florida Atlantic and UCF.
Michigan State Spartans.continuity: Broken. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 3 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 5 — one of the lowest in the guide.
Michigan State Spartans.staff_turnover: Substantial but deliberately mixed. The guide credits a staff blending holdovers for continuity with younger hires, naming former Spartan linebacker Max Bullough, offensive line coach Nick Tabacca and safeties coach James Adams, and separately records special teams coordinator LeVar Woods arriving from Iowa with an assistant head coach title.
Michigan State Spartans.prior_school: Northwestern for Fitzgerald, and the connection is used on the roster too — Fitzgerald turns to NC State transfer Kenny Soares, who played for him at Northwestern, to spark the pass rush. Sheridan comes from Alabama.
Michigan State Spartans.portal_recruiting: Tied to the staff's immediate needs. Five transfers arrive on the offensive line with 72 career starts, including Trent Fraley, the FCS Rimington Award winner at North Dakota State; with 72 sacks allowed over two years, the guide stresses this portal group must gel quickly. Cam Edwards arrives from UConn with 1,240 yards in 2025.
Michigan State Spartans.vsin_assessment: Two positions the guide does not reconcile. The Coaching Carousel says it might be unfair to call a College Football Hall of Famer an underwhelming hire, but that this is an underwhelming hire, and concludes the ceiling in East Lansing feels very low moving forward. The team pages take the other side of the market, arguing it may be underestimating Fitzgerald as a proven programme builder.
Michigan State Spartans.strengths: A College Football Hall of Famer and Northwestern's all-time winningest coach, defensive-coordinator continuity, a staff blending holdovers with younger hires, an established special-teams coordinator brought in from Iowa, and a quarterback situation the guide says should feel better than in several seasons.
Michigan State Spartans.concerns: The circumstances of Fitzgerald's departure from Northwestern and three seasons out of the college game, roster questions across the board, all three top receivers gone, only 22 sacks in 12 games and one returning defensive line starter, and a Stability Score of 5.
Michigan State Spartans.betting: Recommendation is Over 3.5 wins, and the guide says laying around -150 is worth it. The argument is explicitly about the coach: its stated edge is that the market may be underestimating Fitzgerald as a proven programme builder.
Michigan State Spartans.carousel_summary: Adam Burke's assessment is blunt and self-aware: it might be unfair to call a College Football Hall of Famer an underwhelming hire, but this is an underwhelming hire. He records that Fitzgerald was dismissed from Northwestern in 2023 following an investigation into hazing and sexual assault, that a thorough investigation was completed and Fitzgerald was shown the door, and then raises his own counterfactual — whether Fitzgerald would have had more programme support if the team had not gone 1-11 the previous season and 3-9 the season before that. Either way, he writes, Fitzgerald, a volunteer coach at his son's high school for the last three seasons, gets another chance after the aspirational hire of Jonathan Smith did not work out. His conclusion is that the ceiling in East Lansing feels very low moving forward.

Michigan Wolverines.previous_hc_experience: Extensive. The guide records Kyle Whittingham arriving at 66 after 21 seasons and a 177-88 record at Utah, notes he and Utah parted mutually and he wanted to keep coaching, and that this is the first time he has called somewhere other than Salt Lake City home since he was defensive coordinator at Idaho State from 1992-93.
Michigan Wolverines.oc: Jason Beck, with Koy Detmer as quarterbacks coach.
Michigan Wolverines.dc: Jay Hill, former Weber State head coach and three years BYU's coordinator.
Michigan Wolverines.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Michigan Wolverines.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Michigan Wolverines.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The guide attributes the offensive improvement it expects to coordinator Jason Beck.
Michigan Wolverines.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named system. The guide describes Whittingham's identity as old-school, run-first, and focused on physicality along both lines, and records that the staff wants Bryce Underwood running more.
Michigan Wolverines.defensive_scheme: Named. The guide states Michigan will run a 4-2-5 base with varied looks, blitzes and mixed man and zone.
Michigan Wolverines.run_pass: Stated as an identity: old-school and run-first, with the staff wanting more designed running from the quarterback.
Michigan Wolverines.qb_development: Addressed as a coordinator record rather than a head-coach one. The guide expects improvement from coaching alone under Beck and quarterbacks coach Koy Detmer, citing New Mexico's offense going from 44th to fourth nationally in 2024 and Utah's from 115th to fourth last year.
Michigan Wolverines.continuity: Broken across the staff, intact at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 4 for the quarterback, plus 3 for 14 returning starters, totalling 7.
Michigan Wolverines.staff_turnover: Complete at the top. The guide sets it in context: Michigan faced an NCAA investigation into recruiting violations and in-person scouting late in the Jim Harbaugh era, and Harbaugh's successor Sherrone Moore was fired last December over an inappropriate relationship with a staff member. The guide argues no programme is undergoing more cultural change.
Michigan Wolverines.prior_school: Utah, comprehensively — Whittingham, coordinator Jason Beck, and John Henry Daley, a first-team All-American with 11.5 sacks. Jay Hill comes from BYU by way of Weber State, and Chris Bracy arrives from Memphis.
Michigan Wolverines.portal_recruiting: Framed as the difference between Utah and Michigan. The guide says Whittingham achieved discipline, toughness and physicality at Utah by recruiting solid talent and developing it, and that the raw material is now four- and five-stars with a much higher ceiling. It records five-star freshman Savion Hiter behind Jordan Marshall.
Michigan Wolverines.vsin_assessment: Divided between admiration and doubt, and the guide keeps both. The Coaching Carousel calls Whittingham a well-respected, accomplished football lifer brought in to clean up the programme, says he has long been viewed as one of the game's elite coaches both against the spread and in maximizing talent, and that his Utah teams were always tough to face because of their presence in the trenches — then states skepticism about a 66-year-old entering the Big Ten and a programme with extreme expectations. The team pages concede the hire seemed to come out of left field but argue he fits Michigan's identity.
Michigan Wolverines.strengths: A 177-88 record over 21 seasons, a reputation the guide records for maximizing talent and for coaching against the spread, an offensive coordinator with two documented offensive turnarounds, a defensive coordinator who lifted BYU to a top-20 scoring defense, four returning offensive line starters, a talented secondary, and access to recruiting talent well beyond what he had at Utah.
Michigan Wolverines.concerns: Whittingham's age relative to the job as the Carousel frames it, a quarterback the guide calls largely underwhelming statistically, an inexperienced defense with linebacker a stated weakness the guide expects opponents to attack, and a schedule with six ranked opponents including Oklahoma, Iowa, Penn State and Indiana at home plus trips to Oregon and Ohio State.
Michigan Wolverines.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument, though the Coaching Carousel notes Whittingham's long-standing reputation against the spread.
Michigan Wolverines.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames the hire as a cleanup job: Sherrone Moore's ugly departure from Ann Arbor on the heels of Jim Harbaugh's tainted national championship created the need for a well-respected, accomplished football lifer. He notes this is the first time since Whittingham was defensive coordinator at Idaho State in 1992-93 that he calls somewhere other than Salt Lake City home. He then states his own position directly — Whittingham has long been viewed as one of the game's elite coaches, both against the spread and in terms of maximizing talent, and his Utah teams were always tough to face because of their presence in the trenches — before adding that he is skeptical of the 66-year-old entering the Big Ten and a programme with extreme expectations.
